content: Older adults diagnosed with diabetes are at an elevated risk of developing cognitive impairments, which may include memory deficits, difficulties with executive functioning, and dementia. Sustained high blood glucose levels and a longer duration of diabetes are associated with a progressive decline in cognitive abilities. Screening for cognitive impairment in this population should include concise assessment tools, such as the Mini-Mental State Examination, to identify individuals who may require more detailed and comprehensive cognitive evaluations. Cognitive impairments can adversely affect a patient's ability to manage their diabetes care, increasing the likelihood of hypoglycemic episodes and complicating tasks such as medication adherence, dietary planning, and effective glucose monitoring.
